# webcpp::crypto

> Cryptographic primitives for C++20 on native, wasip2, wasip3 and Emscripten: AES-GCM, the AES block cipher, secp256k1 (BIP 340 Schnorr, ECDSA, ECDH, the x-only tweak), Ed25519 and Ed25519ph (RFC 8032), X25519 (RFC 7748), their keys in SPKI, PKCS#8 (RFC 8410) and PEM, libsodium's crypto_kx, the ChaCha20-Poly1305 AEADs, libsodium's secret boxes, boxes and sealed boxes, a random_device on the system's generator and a constant-time equal, each over a widely used, reviewed C library (BearSSL, OpenSSL, ctaes, libsecp256k1, libsodium) that the program names in its Jamfile. Hashing and HMAC are Boost.Hash2's; HKDF and password hashing are webcpp::hash's. Every failure is a boost::system::result value. Protocols (Bitcoin, Ethereum, Nostr) belong to domain libraries built on these primitives.

Generated by doc/tables/generate.py with the page's tables. Page: https://webcpporg.github.io/libs/crypto/

## webcpp::crypto

- [random_device](https://webcpporg.github.io/libs/crypto/#crypto-entropy): Unpredictable bytes from the operating system's or the browser's generator, and nothing else. Header <webcpp/crypto/random_device.hpp>. Backends: the system's generator (/webcpp/crypto//crypto) on native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten. Use it to: generate a session token, a password-reset link or an API key; draw an unbiased number in a range, such as a six-digit code.
  - fill: Fills `output_bytes` from the system's generator.
  - operator(): A value from the system's generator, as the standard library's random device gives one.
  - min: The smallest value `operator()` gives.
  - max: The largest value `operator()` gives.
  - entropy: The entropy of a value, in bits: every bit is the system's.
- [equal](https://webcpporg.github.io/libs/crypto/#crypto-equal): Compares two tags or MACs in constant time. Header <webcpp/crypto/equal.hpp>. Backends: no backend (/webcpp/crypto//crypto) on native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten. Use it to: check a webhook's or an API's HMAC signature.
  - equal: Whether two byte sequences are equal, in a time that does not depend on their contents.
- [error](https://webcpporg.github.io/libs/crypto/#crypto-errors): Every failure's value, fixed and never reused, in the category webcpp.crypto. Header <webcpp/crypto/error.hpp>. Backends: no backend (/webcpp/crypto//crypto) on native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten. Use it to: tell a forged message from a malformed one.
  - error_category: The category of every error.
  - make_error_code: Makes the `error_code` of an error, as its implicit conversion does.
  - message_of: The message of a value of error, or the unknown message for a value it does not define.
- [openssl_memory_resource, backends::openssl::install_memory_functions](https://webcpporg.github.io/libs/crypto/#crypto-memory-openssl): With `WEBCPP_CRYPTO_OPENSSL_MEMORY_RESOURCE`, natively, every allocation of OpenSSL's in the process goes to a `std::pmr::memory_resource` the program defines. Header <webcpp/crypto/backends/openssl.hpp>. Backends: OpenSSL (/webcpp/crypto//openssl) on native. Use it to: keep every allocation of OpenSSL's in the program's arena.
  - openssl_memory_resource: The resource every allocation of OpenSSL's in the process goes to, from any thread: declared by `<webcpp/crypto/backends/openssl.hpp>` under `WEBCPP_CRYPTO_OPENSSL_MEMORY_RESOURCE` and defined once by the program.
  - install_memory_functions: Installs webcpp's adapter as OpenSSL's memory functions, so that every allocation of OpenSSL's in the process goes to `openssl_memory_resource()`.
- [pem::armour, pem::unarmour](https://webcpporg.github.io/libs/crypto/#crypto-key-formats): PEM (RFC 7468): DER as base64 between `-----BEGIN <label>-----` and `-----END <label>-----`, lines of 64 characters and line feeds, as OpenSSL writes it; read strictly, so that any other text is `invalid_encoding`. Header <webcpp/crypto/pem.hpp>. Backends: libsodium (/third_party//sodium) on native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten. Default: libsodium on native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten. Use it to: export or import an Ed25519 or X25519 key in the standard forms OpenSSL and WebCrypto use: SPKI and PKCS#8 (RFC 8410), as DER or PEM text.
  - armour: Writes DER as PEM under a label: `algorithm<Backend>::armour`.
  - unarmour: The DER of PEM under a label, strictly: `algorithm<Backend>::unarmour`.
  - armoured_size: The size of the PEM text of `der_size` bytes under a label of `label_size` characters: its first line, its lines of base64 of 64 characters each with a line feed, and its last line.

## webcpp::crypto::ciphers

- [ciphers::aes128, aes192, aes256](https://webcpporg.github.io/libs/crypto/#crypto-block): The AES block cipher on whole 16-byte blocks: a building block, not encryption of data. Header <webcpp/crypto/ciphers/aes.hpp>. Backends: OpenSSL (/webcpp/crypto//openssl) on native, wasip2, wasip3; ctaes (/third_party//ctaes) on native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten. Default: none on native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten; `aes256<>` takes AES-GCM's default backend as its argument; where that is BearSSL, its `make` does not compile, and the program names `aes256<backends::ctaes>`. Use it to: turn a sequential id into an opaque reference.
  - make: Expands a key.
  - encrypt: Encrypts whole blocks in place.
  - decrypt: Decrypts whole blocks in place.
- [ciphers::gcm, aes128_gcm, aes256_gcm](https://webcpporg.github.io/libs/crypto/#crypto-gcm): AES-GCM, authenticated encryption in place with an incremental seal. Header <webcpp/crypto/ciphers/gcm.hpp>, <webcpp/crypto/ciphers/aes256_gcm.hpp>. Backends: BearSSL (/third_party//bearssl) on native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten; OpenSSL (/webcpp/crypto//openssl) on native, wasip2, wasip3. Default: OpenSSL on native, Clang and GCC; OpenSSL on native, MSVC; BearSSL on wasip2, wasip3; BearSSL on emscripten. Use it to: encrypt a database field, a cookie or a token at rest.
  - make: Expands a key into a new object.
  - seal: Seals a message in place: `data_bytes` holds the plaintext before and the ciphertext after.
  - open: Opens a message in place: `data_bytes` holds the ciphertext before and the plaintext after.
  - begin_seal: Begins an incremental seal: the IV and the whole additional data first, both read before this returns.
  - update: Encrypts the next piece of the message in place.
  - result: Ends the message with its tag.
- [ciphers::chacha20_poly1305](https://webcpporg.github.io/libs/crypto/#crypto-chacha): RFC 8439's ChaCha20-Poly1305, authenticated encryption in place with a 12-byte nonce. Header <webcpp/crypto/ciphers/chacha20_poly1305.hpp>, <webcpp/crypto/ciphers/aead.hpp>. Backends: BearSSL (/third_party//bearssl) on native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten; OpenSSL (/webcpp/crypto//openssl) on native, wasip2, wasip3; libsodium (/third_party//sodium) on native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten. Default: libsodium on native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten.
  - make: Makes an object under a key.
  - seal: Seals a message in place: `data_bytes` holds the plaintext before and the ciphertext after.
  - open: Opens a message in place: `data_bytes` holds the ciphertext before and the plaintext after.
- [ciphers::chacha20_poly1305_original](https://webcpporg.github.io/libs/crypto/#crypto-chacha): The original ChaCha20-Poly1305, authenticated encryption in place with an 8-byte nonce a counter numbers. Header <webcpp/crypto/ciphers/chacha20_poly1305.hpp>, <webcpp/crypto/ciphers/aead.hpp>. Backends: libsodium (/third_party//sodium) on native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten. Default: libsodium on native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten.
  - make: Makes an object under a key.
  - seal: Seals a message in place: `data_bytes` holds the plaintext before and the ciphertext after.
  - open: Opens a message in place: `data_bytes` holds the ciphertext before and the plaintext after.
- [ciphers::xchacha20_poly1305](https://webcpporg.github.io/libs/crypto/#crypto-chacha): XChaCha20-Poly1305, authenticated encryption in place with a 24-byte nonce safe to draw at random. Header <webcpp/crypto/ciphers/chacha20_poly1305.hpp>, <webcpp/crypto/ciphers/aead.hpp>. Backends: libsodium (/third_party//sodium) on native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten. Default: libsodium on native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten. Use it to: encrypt messages in a chat app, on the web and natively, each with a random nonce.
  - make: Makes an object under a key.
  - seal: Seals a message in place: `data_bytes` holds the plaintext before and the ciphertext after.
  - open: Opens a message in place: `data_bytes` holds the ciphertext before and the plaintext after.
- [ciphers::secretbox](https://webcpporg.github.io/libs/crypto/#crypto-secretbox): NaCl's and libsodium's `crypto_secretbox`, XSalsa20-Poly1305: authenticated encryption in place under a 32-byte key, with a 24-byte nonce safe to draw at random and no additional data. Header <webcpp/crypto/ciphers/secretbox.hpp>, <webcpp/crypto/ciphers/aead.hpp>. Backends: libsodium (/third_party//sodium) on native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten. Default: libsodium on native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten. Use it to: encrypt a record or a file under one secret key, each with a random nonce, in libsodium's secret-box format.
  - make: Makes an object under a key.
  - seal: Seals a message in place: `data_bytes` holds the plaintext before and the ciphertext after.
  - open: Opens a message in place: `data_bytes` holds the ciphertext before and the plaintext after.
- [ciphers::secretbox_xchacha20poly1305](https://webcpporg.github.io/libs/crypto/#crypto-secretbox): libsodium's `crypto_secretbox_xchacha20poly1305`: the secret box with XChaCha20 in place of XSalsa20. Header <webcpp/crypto/ciphers/secretbox.hpp>, <webcpp/crypto/ciphers/aead.hpp>. Backends: libsodium (/third_party//sodium) on native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten. Default: libsodium on native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten. Use it to: encrypt a record or a file under one secret key, each with a random nonce, in libsodium's secret-box format.
  - make: Makes an object under a key.
  - seal: Seals a message in place: `data_bytes` holds the plaintext before and the ciphertext after.
  - open: Opens a message in place: `data_bytes` holds the ciphertext before and the plaintext after.

## webcpp::crypto::curves

- [curves::secp256k1::keypair](https://webcpporg.github.io/libs/crypto/#crypto-secp256k1): A secp256k1 key pair: BIP 340 Schnorr and ECDSA signatures, ECDH and the x-only tweak. Header <webcpp/crypto/curves/secp256k1.hpp>. Backends: libsecp256k1 (/third_party//secp256k1) on native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten. Default: libsecp256k1 on native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten.
  - make: Makes a key pair from a secret key.
  - xonly_public_key: The BIP340 x-only public key.
  - public_key: The public key, SEC1 compressed.
  - sign_schnorr: A BIP340 signature of a message of any length.
  - sign_ecdsa: An ECDSA signature of a 32-byte hash: RFC 6979's nonce, low-S, compact form.
  - ecdh: The SHA-256 of the compressed shared point with a peer's public key, libsecp256k1's default.
  - tweak_xonly: Tweaks this key pair in place by a 32-byte tweak t: its x-only public key P becomes P + t*G, and its secret key follows (`secp256k1_keypair_xonly_tweak_add`).
- [curves::secp256k1::verify_schnorr, verify_ecdsa](https://webcpporg.github.io/libs/crypto/#crypto-secp256k1): Verifies a BIP 340 or an ECDSA signature with a public key alone. Header <webcpp/crypto/curves/secp256k1.hpp>. Backends: libsecp256k1 (/third_party//secp256k1) on native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten. Default: libsecp256k1 on native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten.
  - verify_schnorr: Verifies a BIP340 signature with libsecp256k1's static context, which allocates nothing, after its self-test.
  - verify_ecdsa: Verifies an ECDSA signature in compact form with the static context, after its self-test; a high-S signature is refused, as libsecp256k1 refuses it.
- [curves::secp256k1::to_der, from_der, normalize_ecdsa](https://webcpporg.github.io/libs/crypto/#crypto-secp256k1): ECDSA's strict DER encoding and its low-S form. Header <webcpp/crypto/curves/secp256k1.hpp>. Backends: libsecp256k1 (/third_party//secp256k1) on native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten. Default: libsecp256k1 on native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten.
  - to_der: Encodes a compact ECDSA signature as strict DER (BIP66), with libsecp256k1's own encoder.
  - from_der: Decodes a strict DER ECDSA signature (BIP66, `secp256k1_ecdsa_signature_parse_der`) to its compact form.
  - normalize_ecdsa: The low-S form of a compact ECDSA signature (`secp256k1_ecdsa_signature_normalize`), the only form `verify_ecdsa` accepts; a low-S signature is returned unchanged.
- [curves::secp256k1::tweak_xonly](https://webcpporg.github.io/libs/crypto/#crypto-secp256k1): Tweaks an x-only public key by a 32-byte tweak a protocol computes. Header <webcpp/crypto/curves/secp256k1.hpp>. Backends: libsecp256k1 (/third_party//secp256k1) on native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten. Default: libsecp256k1 on native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten.
  - tweak_xonly: Tweaks an x-only public key by a 32-byte tweak t: P + t*G, with libsecp256k1's static context, which allocates nothing (`secp256k1_xonly_pubkey_tweak_add`).
- [curves::ed25519::keypair](https://webcpporg.github.io/libs/crypto/#crypto-ed25519): An Ed25519 key pair (RFC 8032): made from a 32-byte seed or drawn from `random_device`, its 32-byte public key, 64-byte signatures, and its X25519 secret key. Header <webcpp/crypto/curves/ed25519.hpp>. Backends: libsodium (/third_party//sodium) on native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten. Default: libsodium on native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten. Use it to: sign and verify with Ed25519 (RFC 8032), or sign a large message in pieces with Ed25519ph.
  - make: Makes a key pair from a seed, RFC 8032's secret key.
  - generate: Makes a key pair from a fresh seed, drawn from the system's generator.
  - public_key: The public key.
  - sign: Signs a message.
  - x25519_secret: The X25519 secret key of this key pair, RFC 7748's form of the clamped first half of the seed's SHA-512.
- [curves::ed25519::verify](https://webcpporg.github.io/libs/crypto/#crypto-ed25519): Verifies an Ed25519 signature with a public key alone, under the policy `strict`: libsodium's rules, which refuse non-canonical encodings and keys of small order. Header <webcpp/crypto/curves/ed25519.hpp>. Backends: libsodium (/third_party//sodium) on native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten. Default: libsodium on native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten. Use it to: sign and verify with Ed25519 (RFC 8032), or sign a large message in pieces with Ed25519ph.
  - verify: Verifies an Ed25519 signature under a verification policy (design D31).
- [curves::ed25519::ph](https://webcpporg.github.io/libs/crypto/#crypto-ed25519): Ed25519ph (RFC 8032): a message given in pieces, hashed with SHA-512, then signed with a key pair or verified with a public key. Header <webcpp/crypto/curves/ed25519.hpp>. Backends: libsodium (/third_party//sodium) on native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten. Default: libsodium on native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten. Use it to: sign and verify with Ed25519 (RFC 8032), or sign a large message in pieces with Ed25519ph.
  - begin: Begins a message.
  - update: Adds a piece of the message.
  - sign: Signs the message given, which it ends.
  - verify: Verifies a signature of the message given, which it ends, strictly (design D31).
- [curves::ed25519::to_x25519_public](https://webcpporg.github.io/libs/crypto/#crypto-x25519): The X25519 public key of an Ed25519 public key (the birational map), refusing a key of small order or not canonical with `invalid_public_key`. Header <webcpp/crypto/curves/ed25519.hpp>. Backends: libsodium (/third_party//sodium) on native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten. Default: libsodium on native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten. Use it to: agree a shared secret with a peer's public key (X25519, RFC 7748), or with the X25519 form of an Ed25519 key.
  - to_x25519_public: The X25519 public key of an Ed25519 public key (the birational map from edwards25519 to Curve25519), so that a peer known by its Ed25519 key can be agreed with by `curves::x25519::agree`; the key pair's own side is `basic_keypair::x25519_secret`.
- [curves::x25519::public_key](https://webcpporg.github.io/libs/crypto/#crypto-x25519): The 32-byte X25519 public key of a 32-byte secret key (RFC 7748). Header <webcpp/crypto/curves/x25519.hpp>. Backends: libsodium (/third_party//sodium) on native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten. Default: libsodium on native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten. Use it to: agree a shared secret with a peer's public key (X25519, RFC 7748), or with the X25519 form of an Ed25519 key.
  - public_key: The public key of a secret key: `algorithm<Backend>::public_key`.
- [curves::x25519::agree](https://webcpporg.github.io/libs/crypto/#crypto-x25519): The 32-byte shared secret of a secret key and a peer's public key, a `secret<32>`, refused with `weak_public_key` when it is all zero (a peer key of low order). Header <webcpp/crypto/curves/x25519.hpp>. Backends: libsodium (/third_party//sodium) on native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten. Default: libsodium on native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten. Use it to: agree a shared secret with a peer's public key (X25519, RFC 7748), or with the X25519 form of an Ed25519 key.
  - agree: The shared secret, refused when all zero: `algorithm<Backend>::agree`.
- [curves::ed25519::encode_spki, decode_spki, encode_pkcs8, decode_pkcs8](https://webcpporg.github.io/libs/crypto/#crypto-key-formats): RFC 8410's SPKI of an Ed25519 public key (44 bytes) and PKCS#8 of a key pair (version 1, the seed alone, 48 bytes), the forms OpenSSL and WebCrypto write, decoded strictly: any other bytes are `invalid_encoding`. Header <webcpp/crypto/curves/ed25519/formats.hpp>. Backends: libsodium (/third_party//sodium) on native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten. Default: libsodium on native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten. Use it to: export or import an Ed25519 or X25519 key in the standard forms OpenSSL and WebCrypto use: SPKI and PKCS#8 (RFC 8410), as DER or PEM text.
  - encode_spki: Writes a public key's SPKI (RFC 8410) into `out`.
  - decode_spki: The public key of an SPKI, refused unless it is exactly RFC 8410's form: the 12 bytes of Ed25519's prefix, then the key, and nothing after.
  - encode_pkcs8: Writes a key pair's PKCS#8 (RFC 8410, version 1: the seed, without the public key) into `out`, which then holds the secret key: a program wipes it, or seals it, when it is done.
  - decode_pkcs8: The key pair of a PKCS#8, refused unless it is exactly RFC 8410's version 1 form: the 16 bytes of Ed25519's prefix, then the seed, and nothing after.
- [curves::x25519::encode_spki, decode_spki, encode_pkcs8, decode_pkcs8](https://webcpporg.github.io/libs/crypto/#crypto-key-formats): RFC 8410's SPKI of an X25519 public key (44 bytes) and PKCS#8 of a secret key (version 1, 48 bytes), the forms OpenSSL and WebCrypto write, decoded strictly into a `secret<32>`: any other bytes are `invalid_encoding`. Header <webcpp/crypto/curves/x25519/formats.hpp>. Backends: libsodium (/third_party//sodium) on native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten. Default: libsodium on native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten. Use it to: export or import an Ed25519 or X25519 key in the standard forms OpenSSL and WebCrypto use: SPKI and PKCS#8 (RFC 8410), as DER or PEM text.
  - encode_spki: Writes a public key's SPKI (RFC 8410) into `out`.
  - decode_spki: The public key of an SPKI, refused unless it is exactly RFC 8410's form: the 12 bytes of X25519's prefix, then the key, and nothing after.
  - encode_pkcs8: Writes a secret key's PKCS#8 (RFC 8410, version 1: the secret key, without the public key) into `out`, which then holds the secret key: a program wipes it, or seals it, when it is done.
  - decode_pkcs8: The secret key of a PKCS#8, refused unless it is exactly RFC 8410's version 1 form: the 16 bytes of X25519's prefix, then the secret key, and nothing after.
- [curves::x25519::kx_keypair](https://webcpporg.github.io/libs/crypto/#crypto-kx): libsodium's `crypto_kx`: a key pair made from a 32-byte seed or drawn from `random_device`, and the two session keys of a client or a server, each a `secret<32>`, from the peer's public key; a peer key of low order is refused with `weak_public_key`. Header <webcpp/crypto/curves/x25519/kx.hpp>. Backends: libsodium (/third_party//sodium) on native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten. Default: libsodium on native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten. Use it to: give a client and a server a key for each direction from each other's public key, as libsodium's `crypto_kx` does.
  - make: Makes a key pair from a seed, `crypto_kx_seed_keypair`: the same seed gives the same key pair.
  - generate: Makes a key pair from a fresh seed, drawn from the system's generator.
  - public_key: The public key, which the peer needs.
  - client_session_keys: The client's keys, from the server's public key, `crypto_kx_client_session_keys`.
  - server_session_keys: The server's keys, from the client's public key, `crypto_kx_server_session_keys`.

## webcpp::crypto::hybrid

- [hybrid::box](https://webcpporg.github.io/libs/crypto/#crypto-box): NaCl's and libsodium's `crypto_box`: X25519 agrees a key once per pair of keys, refusing a peer key of small order, then XSalsa20-Poly1305 seals and opens each message in place, with a 24-byte nonce safe to draw at random. Header <webcpp/crypto/hybrid/box.hpp>. Backends: libsodium (/third_party//sodium) on native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten. Default: libsodium on native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten. Use it to: send messages between two people who know each other's public keys, as NaCl's and libsodium's crypto_box.
  - make: Agrees the box's key from the own secret key and the peer's public key.
  - seal: Seals a message in place: `data_bytes` holds the plaintext before and the ciphertext after.
  - open: Opens a message in place: `data_bytes` holds the ciphertext before and the plaintext after.
- [hybrid::box_xchacha20poly1305](https://webcpporg.github.io/libs/crypto/#crypto-box): libsodium's `crypto_box_curve25519xchacha20poly1305`: the box with XChaCha20 in place of XSalsa20. Header <webcpp/crypto/hybrid/box.hpp>. Backends: libsodium (/third_party//sodium) on native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten. Default: libsodium on native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten.
  - make: Agrees the box's key from the own secret key and the peer's public key.
  - seal: Seals a message in place: `data_bytes` holds the plaintext before and the ciphertext after.
  - open: Opens a message in place: `data_bytes` holds the ciphertext before and the plaintext after.
- [hybrid::sealed_box](https://webcpporg.github.io/libs/crypto/#crypto-sealed-box): libsodium's sealed boxes, `crypto_box_seal`: anonymous encryption to a public key under a key pair drawn per message, 48 bytes longer than the message, which only the recipient's key pair opens. Header <webcpp/crypto/hybrid/sealed_box.hpp>. Backends: libsodium (/third_party//sodium) on native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten. Default: libsodium on native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten. Use it to: let anyone send a message that only the recipient can read, without saying who sent it (anonymous feedback, a drop box).
  - seal: Seals `message` into `out`, of `message.size() + overhead` bytes: the drawn public key, the tag, then the ciphertext.
  - open: Opens `sealed` into `out`, of `sealed.size() - overhead` bytes, with the recipient's keys.

## Default backend per family

- AES-GCM, native, Clang and GCC: OpenSSL; OpenSSL's assembly uses the CPU's AES and carry-less multiplication instructions on x86-64 and ARMv8 ([OpenSSL's AES assembly for ARMv8 and x86-64](https://github.com/openssl/openssl/tree/master/crypto/aes/asm); [OpenSSL's GHASH and AES-GCM assembly](https://github.com/openssl/openssl/tree/master/crypto/modes/asm)); BearSSL has them on x86 only ([BearSSL, the AES implementations it selects](https://www.bearssl.org/support.html)). OpenSSL whatever the program links: a program that links BearSSL alone names `gcm<aes256<backends::bearssl>>`.
- AES-GCM, native, MSVC: OpenSSL; the same rule as with Clang and GCC, but here OpenSSL is built no-asm: table-based AES and 4-bit GHASH, no AES-NI, not constant time ([OpenSSL's INSTALL.md, no-asm](https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/master/INSTALL.md)); where timing attacks matter, link BearSSL and name `gcm<aes256<backends::bearssl>>`.
- AES-GCM, wasip2, wasip3: BearSSL; constant time by design ([BearSSL, constant-time crypto](https://www.bearssl.org/constanttime.html)), where OpenSSL is built no-asm and its AES and GHASH are table-based ([OpenSSL's INSTALL.md, no-asm](https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/master/INSTALL.md)). BearSSL whatever the program links: a program that links OpenSSL alone names `gcm<aes256<backends::openssl>>`.
- AES-GCM, emscripten: BearSSL; the only AES-GCM backend there: webcpp does not build OpenSSL for Emscripten.
- AES block cipher, native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten: none; a raw block cipher is a building block a program chooses deliberately, naming its backend; `aes256<>` takes AES-GCM's default as its argument, and its `make` does not compile where that is BearSSL.
- secp256k1, native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten: libsecp256k1; the only backend ([libsecp256k1's README](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/secp256k1#readme)).
- Ed25519, native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten: libsodium; the only backend in this version, on every target, and its verification is the policy `strict` ([libsodium's documentation, public-key signatures](https://doc.libsodium.org/public-key_cryptography/public-key_signatures); [RFC 8032, the Edwards-curve Digital Signature Algorithm (EdDSA)](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8032)).
- X25519, native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten: libsodium; the only backend in this version, on every target; it refuses an all-zero shared secret itself ([RFC 7748, Elliptic Curves for Security (X25519 and X448)](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7748)).
- crypto_kx, native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten: libsodium; the only backend that has it: libsodium's own construction, whose session keys only another `crypto_kx` derives ([libsodium's documentation, key exchange](https://doc.libsodium.org/key_exchange)).
- PEM, native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten: libsodium; the only backend in this version, on every target; its base64 runs in a time that does not depend on the bytes, a private key's in a PKCS#8 ([libsodium's documentation, helpers: base64 encoding and decoding](https://doc.libsodium.org/helpers#base64-encoding-decoding)).
- ChaCha20-Poly1305, native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten: libsodium; one library for the three ChaCha20-Poly1305 AEADs on every target, where BearSSL and OpenSSL have RFC 8439's alone ([libsodium's ChaCha20-Poly1305 constructions](https://doc.libsodium.org/secret-key_cryptography/aead/chacha20-poly1305)); a program that links BearSSL or OpenSSL alone names it in the type, as in `chacha20_poly1305<backends::bearssl>`.
- original ChaCha20-Poly1305, native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten: libsodium; the only backend that has it: libsodium's own C code, the same on every target ([libsodium's ChaCha20-Poly1305 constructions](https://doc.libsodium.org/secret-key_cryptography/aead/chacha20-poly1305)).
- XChaCha20-Poly1305, native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten: libsodium; the only backend that has it: libsodium's own C code, the same on every target ([libsodium's ChaCha20-Poly1305 constructions](https://doc.libsodium.org/secret-key_cryptography/aead/chacha20-poly1305)).
- XSalsa20-Poly1305 secret box, native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten: libsodium; the only backend that has it: libsodium's own C code, NaCl's `crypto_secretbox`, the same on every target ([libsodium's documentation, secret-key authenticated encryption](https://doc.libsodium.org/secret-key_cryptography/secretbox)).
- XChaCha20-Poly1305 secret box, native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten: libsodium; the only backend that has it: libsodium's own C code, the same on every target ([libsodium's documentation, secret-key authenticated encryption](https://doc.libsodium.org/secret-key_cryptography/secretbox)).
- X25519-XSalsa20-Poly1305 box, native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten: libsodium; the only backend that has it: libsodium's own C code, NaCl's `crypto_box`, the same on every target ([libsodium's documentation, public-key authenticated encryption](https://doc.libsodium.org/public-key_cryptography/authenticated_encryption)).
- X25519-XChaCha20-Poly1305 box, native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten: libsodium; the only backend that has it: libsodium's own C code, the same on every target ([libsodium's documentation, public-key authenticated encryption](https://doc.libsodium.org/public-key_cryptography/authenticated_encryption)).
- X25519-XSalsa20-Poly1305 sealed box, native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten: libsodium; the only backend that has it: libsodium's own C code, which draws the key pair of each message from its own generator, the same on every target ([libsodium's documentation, sealed boxes](https://doc.libsodium.org/public-key_cryptography/sealed_boxes)).

## Constant time, measured

- AES-GCM: BearSSL: native, Valgrind's memcheck (Linux), MemorySanitizer (Linux, clang) and dudect, nothing found; wasip2, dudect, nothing found; not measured yet on wasip3, emscripten. OpenSSL (seal alone: its open branches on the verdict inside OpenSSL): native, Valgrind's memcheck (Linux), nothing found; not measured yet on wasip2, wasip3.
- AES block cipher: OpenSSL: not measured yet. ctaes: native, Valgrind's memcheck (Linux), MemorySanitizer (Linux, clang) and dudect, nothing found; wasip2, dudect, nothing found; not measured yet on wasip3, emscripten.
- secp256k1: libsecp256k1 (libsecp256k1's own `ctime_tests.c`): native, Valgrind's memcheck (Linux) and MemorySanitizer (Linux, clang), nothing found; not measured yet on wasip2, wasip3, emscripten.
- Ed25519: libsodium: native, Valgrind's memcheck (Linux), MemorySanitizer (Linux, clang) and dudect, nothing found; wasip2, dudect, nothing found; not measured yet on wasip3, emscripten.
- X25519: libsodium: native, Valgrind's memcheck (Linux), MemorySanitizer (Linux, clang) and dudect: nothing found with arm64's DIT (data-independent timing) bit set, as the lane runs dudect and as Apple requires of constant-time code ([Apple, Writing ARM64 code for Apple platforms: enable DIT for constant-time cryptographic operations](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/xcode/writing-arm64-code-for-apple-platforms#Enable-DIT-for-constant-time-cryptographic-operations)); without it, dudect times `agree` with an all-zero secret key against random ones at |t| 6.7 to 14.5, against the threshold 10, on an Apple M5 Max, from a release build (2026-11-19): about one nanosecond in 15 µs. libsodium does not set DIT: a program on Apple silicon sets it around its secret operations ([Apple, Writing ARM64 code for Apple platforms: enable DIT for constant-time cryptographic operations](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/xcode/writing-arm64-code-for-apple-platforms#Enable-DIT-for-constant-time-cryptographic-operations)); wasip2, dudect: an open finding, its cause measured: dudect times `agree` with an all-zero secret key against random ones at |t| 13 to 32 (2026-11-18; a fixed key against another fixed key: 22.9) and 107 to 260 (2026-11-19), against the threshold 10, under wasmtime 47 on an Apple M5 Max, from a release build. The cause is Apple silicon's DIT (data-independent timing), which wasmtime does not set ([Apple, Writing ARM64 code for Apple platforms: enable DIT for constant-time cryptographic operations](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/xcode/writing-arm64-code-for-apple-platforms#Enable-DIT-for-constant-time-cryptographic-operations)): with DIT set in wasmtime's main thread, an experiment and not the lane, the same case reads |t| 1.5 to 2.1; no branch on a secret was found in the WebAssembly or in wasmtime's compiled code. The lane cannot set DIT from inside the WebAssembly, so it prints this value on wasip2 without judging it; the CI's x86-64 run measures it next; not measured yet on wasip3, emscripten.
- crypto_kx: libsodium: native, Valgrind's memcheck (Linux) and MemorySanitizer (Linux, clang), nothing found; not measured yet on wasip2, wasip3, emscripten.
- PEM: libsodium: not measured yet.
- ChaCha20-Poly1305: libsodium: native, Valgrind's memcheck (Linux) and MemorySanitizer (Linux, clang), nothing found; not measured yet on wasip2, wasip3, emscripten. BearSSL: native, Valgrind's memcheck (Linux), MemorySanitizer (Linux, clang) and dudect, nothing found; wasip2, dudect, nothing found; not measured yet on wasip3, emscripten. OpenSSL (seal alone: its open branches on the verdict inside OpenSSL): native, Valgrind's memcheck (Linux), nothing found; not measured yet on wasip2, wasip3.
- original ChaCha20-Poly1305: libsodium: native, Valgrind's memcheck (Linux) and MemorySanitizer (Linux, clang), nothing found; not measured yet on wasip2, wasip3, emscripten.
- XChaCha20-Poly1305: libsodium: native, Valgrind's memcheck (Linux) and MemorySanitizer (Linux, clang), nothing found; not measured yet on wasip2, wasip3, emscripten.
- XSalsa20-Poly1305 secret box: libsodium: native, Valgrind's memcheck (Linux) and MemorySanitizer (Linux, clang), nothing found; not measured yet on wasip2, wasip3, emscripten.
- XChaCha20-Poly1305 secret box: libsodium: native, Valgrind's memcheck (Linux) and MemorySanitizer (Linux, clang), nothing found; not measured yet on wasip2, wasip3, emscripten.
- X25519-XSalsa20-Poly1305 box: libsodium: native, Valgrind's memcheck (Linux) and MemorySanitizer (Linux, clang), nothing found; not measured yet on wasip2, wasip3, emscripten.
- X25519-XChaCha20-Poly1305 box: libsodium: native, Valgrind's memcheck (Linux) and MemorySanitizer (Linux, clang), nothing found; not measured yet on wasip2, wasip3, emscripten.
- X25519-XSalsa20-Poly1305 sealed box: libsodium: native, Valgrind's memcheck (Linux) and MemorySanitizer (Linux, clang), nothing found; not measured yet on wasip2, wasip3, emscripten.

## Rules of use

- [Never reuse an IV under one key](https://webcpporg.github.io/libs/crypto/#crypto-gcm-rules): two AES-GCM messages under one key and one IV reveal the XOR of their plaintexts and let an attacker forge tags for every later message ([A. Joux, Authentication Failures in NIST version of GCM, 2006](https://csrc.nist.gov/csrc/media/projects/block-cipher-techniques/documents/bcm/comments/800-38-series-drafts/gcm/joux_comments.pdf); [H. Boeck et al., Nonce-Disrespecting Adversaries, 2016](https://eprint.iacr.org/2016/475)); draw a random 12-byte IV per message, or use a counter that never repeats, a restart included.
- [The usage limit](https://webcpporg.github.io/libs/crypto/#crypto-gcm-rules): with random IVs, at most 2^32 messages under one key ([NIST SP 800-38D, GCM and GMAC](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/38/d/final), section 8.3); rotate the key before.
- [A failed open zeroes data](https://webcpporg.github.io/libs/crypto/#crypto-gcm-rules): when the tag does not match, `open` returns `authentication_failed` and zeroes the whole of `data`; keep a copy of the ciphertext if it is needed after a failure. There is no incremental open: a large message is split into records.
- [Records: each stream its own key](https://webcpporg.github.io/libs/crypto/#crypto-gcm-incremental): records numbered from 0 with the number as IV are safe only under a key used for that one stream: derive a key per stream (HKDF of the storage key with a random salt) or draw one; never number two streams' records under one key.
- [ECDH's form](https://webcpporg.github.io/libs/crypto/#crypto-secp256k1): `keypair::ecdh` returns libsecp256k1's hashed form, the SHA-256 of the compressed shared point; it does not interoperate with protocols that take the raw x coordinate, such as Nostr's NIP-44 ([Nostr NIP-44, encrypted payloads](https://github.com/nostr-protocol/nips/blob/master/44.md)). Derive keys from it with HKDF, never use it directly.
- [The x-only tweak is not BIP 32](https://webcpporg.github.io/libs/crypto/#crypto-wallets-taproot): `tweak_xonly` is BIP 341's even-y arithmetic ([BIP 341, Taproot](https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/blob/master/bip-0341.mediawiki)); BIP 32's child derivation needs a tweak of the full key, which this version does not offer ([BIP 32, hierarchical deterministic wallets](https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/blob/master/bip-0032.mediawiki)).
- [Ethereum](https://webcpporg.github.io/libs/crypto/#crypto-curves): this version verifies Ethereum's ECDSA signatures with a known key but has no recoverable signature (no recovery id `v`, no public key recovery) and no uncompressed public key output, so it cannot sign Ethereum transactions or derive addresses.
- [Compare secrets in constant time](https://webcpporg.github.io/libs/crypto/#crypto-equal): compare a tag, a MAC or a token with `equal`, never `==` or `memcmp` ([CWE-208, observable timing discrepancy](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/208.html)).
- [Secrets come from random_device](https://webcpporg.github.io/libs/crypto/#crypto-entropy): keys, IVs and tokens are drawn from `random_device`, never `std::mt19937` or `rand` ([CWE-338, a weak generator used for security](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/338.html)).
- [Never reuse a nonce under one ChaCha20-Poly1305 key](https://webcpporg.github.io/libs/crypto/#crypto-chacha): two messages under one key and one nonce reveal the XOR of their plaintexts and let an attacker forge tags ([RFC 8439, section 4: a nonce is never repeated under one key](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8439#section-4)). `xchacha20_poly1305` and the secret boxes: draw 24 bytes at random per message. `chacha20_poly1305`: number the 12-byte nonces with a counter that never repeats, a restart included, or draw them at random for at most 2^32 messages per key, AES-GCM's bound for random 12-byte IVs ([NIST SP 800-38D, GCM and GMAC](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/38/d/final)). `chacha20_poly1305_original`: a counter only, its 8 bytes are too short to draw.
- [A shared secret is not a key](https://webcpporg.github.io/libs/crypto/#crypto-x25519): derive keys from X25519's shared secret and both public keys with a KDF such as webcpp::hash's HKDF, never use its bytes as a cipher's key ([RFC 7748, section 6.1: a KDF over the shared secret and both public keys](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7748#section-6.1)); `kx_keypair` and the boxes do this themselves.
- [The default on MSVC is not constant time](https://webcpporg.github.io/libs/crypto/#crypto-backends-defaults): natively the default is OpenSSL, which MSVC builds no-asm, table-based ([OpenSSL's INSTALL.md, no-asm](https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/master/INSTALL.md)); where timing attacks matter, link BearSSL and name `gcm<aes256<backends::bearssl>>`.

## Choose by use case

- [Generate a session token, a password-reset link or an API key](https://webcpporg.github.io/libs/crypto/#crypto-entropy): `random_device::fill` (webcpp::crypto); backend the system's generator; Jamfile /webcpp/crypto//crypto. Example: example/reset_token.cpp.
- [Draw an unbiased number in a range, such as a six-digit code](https://webcpporg.github.io/libs/crypto/#crypto-entropy): `random_device` with `std::uniform_int_distribution` (webcpp::crypto); backend the system's generator; Jamfile /webcpp/crypto//crypto. Example: example/reset_token.cpp.
- [Check a webhook's or an API's HMAC signature](https://webcpporg.github.io/libs/crypto/#crypto-equal): `equal`, with Boost.Hash2's `hmac` (webcpp::crypto); backend none; Jamfile /webcpp/crypto//crypto. Example: example/equal_hmac.cpp.
- [Encrypt a database field, a cookie or a token at rest](https://webcpporg.github.io/libs/crypto/#crypto-gcm): `aes256_gcm` (webcpp::crypto::ciphers); backend the default: OpenSSL natively, BearSSL on WebAssembly; Jamfile /webcpp/crypto//crypto /webcpp/crypto//gcm-default. Example: example/store_token.cpp.
- [Encrypt a large file or a stream](https://webcpporg.github.io/libs/crypto/#crypto-gcm-incremental): `aes256_gcm`: records, or `begin_seal`, `update` and `result` (webcpp::crypto::ciphers); backend the default; Jamfile /webcpp/crypto//crypto /webcpp/crypto//gcm-default. Example: example/sealed_records.cpp.
- [Tell a forged message from a malformed one](https://webcpporg.github.io/libs/crypto/#crypto-errors): `error` (webcpp::crypto); backend any; Jamfile /webcpp/crypto//crypto. Example: example/failure_reasons.cpp.
- [Turn a sequential id into an opaque reference](https://webcpporg.github.io/libs/crypto/#crypto-block): `aes256<backends::ctaes>` (webcpp::crypto::ciphers); backend ctaes, or OpenSSL natively and on WASI; Jamfile /webcpp/crypto//crypto /third_party//ctaes. Example: example/order_reference.cpp.
- [Prove who wrote a message posted to a relay](https://webcpporg.github.io/libs/crypto/#crypto-p2p-signed): `keypair::sign_schnorr`, `verify_schnorr` (webcpp::crypto::curves::secp256k1); backend libsecp256k1; Jamfile /webcpp/crypto//crypto /third_party//secp256k1. Example: example/signed_message.cpp.
- [Check a software update or a licence file](https://webcpporg.github.io/libs/crypto/#crypto-everyday-update): `keypair::sign_ecdsa`, `verify_ecdsa` (webcpp::crypto::curves::secp256k1); backend libsecp256k1; Jamfile /webcpp/crypto//crypto /third_party//secp256k1. Example: example/signed_update.cpp.
- [Agree on a key with a peer through a relay that sees everything](https://webcpporg.github.io/libs/crypto/#crypto-p2p-session): `keypair::ecdh` (SHA-256 of the shared point: not NIP-44's raw x coordinate), then HKDF on Boost.Hash2 and `aes256_gcm` (webcpp::crypto::curves::secp256k1); backend libsecp256k1, and AES-GCM's default; Jamfile /webcpp/crypto//crypto /third_party//secp256k1 /webcpp/crypto//gcm-default. Example: example/ecdh_session.cpp.
- [Make and keep a wallet's key](https://webcpporg.github.io/libs/crypto/#crypto-wallets-key): `keypair::make`, `xonly_public_key`, `public_key`; `aes256_gcm` at rest (webcpp::crypto::curves::secp256k1); backend libsecp256k1, and AES-GCM's default; Jamfile /webcpp/crypto//crypto /third_party//secp256k1 /webcpp/crypto//gcm-default. Example: example/wallet_key.cpp.
- [Sign a Bitcoin SegWit v0 input (a domain library's job)](https://webcpporg.github.io/libs/crypto/#crypto-wallets-der): `sign_ecdsa`, `to_der`, `normalize_ecdsa` (webcpp::crypto::curves::secp256k1); backend libsecp256k1; Jamfile /webcpp/crypto//crypto /third_party//secp256k1. Example: example/ecdsa_der.cpp.
- [Derive a Bitcoin Taproot output key and spend by key path (a domain library's job)](https://webcpporg.github.io/libs/crypto/#crypto-wallets-taproot): `tweak_xonly`, `keypair::tweak_xonly` (webcpp::crypto::curves::secp256k1); backend libsecp256k1; Jamfile /webcpp/crypto//crypto /third_party//secp256k1. Example: example/taproot_tweak.cpp.
- [Sign where allocation is restricted to the program's arena](https://webcpporg.github.io/libs/crypto/#crypto-memory): `keypair::make(secret, resource)` (webcpp::crypto::curves::secp256k1); backend libsecp256k1; Jamfile /webcpp/crypto//crypto /third_party//secp256k1. Example: example/arena_signer.cpp.
- [Keep every allocation of OpenSSL's in the program's arena](https://webcpporg.github.io/libs/crypto/#crypto-memory-openssl): `openssl_memory_resource`, `backends::openssl::install_memory_functions` (webcpp::crypto); backend OpenSSL, natively; Jamfile `/webcpp/crypto//crypto` in the program; in the project requirements, `<define>WEBCPP_CRYPTO_OPENSSL_MEMORY_RESOURCE` and `<library>/webcpp/crypto//openssl`. Example: example/openssl_memory.cpp.
- [Seed BearSSL's own generator for code that calls BearSSL directly](https://webcpporg.github.io/libs/crypto/#crypto-entropy-bearssl): `random_device::fill` (webcpp::crypto); backend BearSSL's C API; Jamfile /webcpp/crypto//crypto /third_party//bearssl. Example: example/bearssl_prng.cpp.
- [Hash, or compute an HMAC](https://webcpporg.github.io/libs/crypto/#crypto-overview-hash2): `boost::hash2::sha2_256`, `hmac_sha2_256` (Boost.Hash2, not this library); backend none; Jamfile `/webcpp/crypto//crypto` brings Boost's headers. Example: example/equal_hmac.cpp.
- [Sign and verify with Ed25519 (RFC 8032), or sign a large message in pieces with Ed25519ph](https://webcpporg.github.io/libs/crypto/#crypto-ed25519): `keypair::make`, `keypair::generate`, `keypair::sign`, `verify`; `ph<webcpp::hash::sha2_512>` (webcpp::crypto::curves::ed25519); backend libsodium; Jamfile /webcpp/crypto//crypto /webcpp/crypto//ed25519-default. Example: example/ed25519_sign.cpp.
- [Agree a shared secret with a peer's public key (X25519, RFC 7748), or with the X25519 form of an Ed25519 key](https://webcpporg.github.io/libs/crypto/#crypto-x25519): `public_key`, `agree`; `curves::ed25519::to_x25519_public`, `curves::ed25519::keypair::x25519_secret` (webcpp::crypto::curves::x25519); backend libsodium; Jamfile /webcpp/crypto//crypto /webcpp/crypto//x25519-default. Example: example/x25519_agree.cpp.
- [Give a client and a server a key for each direction from each other's public key, as libsodium's `crypto_kx` does](https://webcpporg.github.io/libs/crypto/#crypto-kx): `kx_keypair::make`, `kx_keypair::generate`, `client_session_keys`, `server_session_keys` (webcpp::crypto::curves::x25519); backend libsodium; Jamfile /webcpp/crypto//crypto /webcpp/crypto//kx-default. Example: example/kx_session.cpp.
- [Export or import an Ed25519 or X25519 key in the standard forms OpenSSL and WebCrypto use: SPKI and PKCS#8 (RFC 8410), as DER or PEM text](https://webcpporg.github.io/libs/crypto/#crypto-key-formats): `ed25519::encode_spki`, `decode_spki`, `encode_pkcs8`, `decode_pkcs8`, the same in `x25519`; `webcpp::crypto::pem::armour`, `unarmour` (webcpp::crypto::curves); backend libsodium; Jamfile /webcpp/crypto//crypto /webcpp/crypto//ed25519-default /webcpp/crypto//x25519-default /webcpp/crypto//pem-default. Example: example/key_formats.cpp.
- [Encrypt messages in a chat app, on the web and natively, each with a random nonce](https://webcpporg.github.io/libs/crypto/#crypto-chacha): `xchacha20_poly1305<>`: `make`, `seal`, `open` (webcpp::crypto::ciphers); backend libsodium; Jamfile /webcpp/crypto//crypto /webcpp/crypto//xchacha20_poly1305-default. Example: example/xchacha_seal.cpp.
- [Encrypt a record or a file under one secret key, each with a random nonce, in libsodium's secret-box format](https://webcpporg.github.io/libs/crypto/#crypto-secretbox): `secretbox<>`, `secretbox_xchacha20poly1305<>`: `make`, `seal`, `open` (webcpp::crypto::ciphers); backend libsodium; Jamfile /webcpp/crypto//crypto /webcpp/crypto//secretbox_xsalsa20poly1305-default. Example: example/file_share.cpp.
- [Send messages between two people who know each other's public keys, as NaCl's and libsodium's crypto_box](https://webcpporg.github.io/libs/crypto/#crypto-box): `box::make`, `box::seal`, `box::open` (webcpp::crypto::hybrid); backend libsodium; Jamfile /webcpp/crypto//crypto /webcpp/crypto//box_xsalsa20poly1305-default. Example: example/box_messages.cpp.
- [Let anyone send a message that only the recipient can read, without saying who sent it (anonymous feedback, a drop box)](https://webcpporg.github.io/libs/crypto/#crypto-sealed-box): `sealed_box::seal`, `sealed_box::open` (webcpp::crypto::hybrid); backend libsodium; Jamfile /webcpp/crypto//crypto /webcpp/crypto//sealed_box-default. Example: example/file_share.cpp.
- [Share a file with someone known only by a public key, as a file-sharing app does](https://webcpporg.github.io/libs/crypto/#crypto-everyday-files): `ciphers::secretbox<>` for the file under a key drawn for it, `hybrid::sealed_box::seal` for that key (webcpp::crypto); backend libsodium; Jamfile /webcpp/crypto//crypto /webcpp/crypto//secretbox_xsalsa20poly1305-default /webcpp/crypto//sealed_box-default /webcpp/crypto//x25519-default. Example: example/file_share.cpp.
- [Use P-256 (passkeys, JWT's ES256)](https://webcpporg.github.io/libs/crypto/#crypto-curves): secp256k1, Ed25519 and X25519 keys and signatures do not interoperate with this curve (none in this version); backend none; Jamfile none.

## Examples

- example/aes256_gcm_bearssl.cpp: Seals one zero block with AES-256-GCM on BearSSL, names the backend in the type, checks the result against test case 14 of the GCM specification, and opens it again. Naming the backend pins the implementation, so the same bytes and the same code run on every target.
- example/arena_signer.cpp: Gives the secp256k1 key pair its one allocation from a fixed buffer owned by the program, and counts it. With a null upstream nothing else can allocate, so a program with strict memory limits knows exactly what the library needs and that it never reaches for the heap.
- example/bearssl_prng.cpp: Seeds BearSSL's own HMAC-DRBG from webcpp::crypto::random_device and draws bytes from it. A generator is only as good as its seed: the seed must come from the system's entropy, never from the clock or a counter.
- example/box_messages.cpp: Two people who know each other's X25519 public keys exchange messages in libsodium's box: each makes a box from the own secret key and the other's public key, agreeing one key for the pair, then seals each message with a nonce drawn at random. What one seals the other opens; a stranger's box, from another key pair, does not. Prints what each reads.
- example/ecdh_session.cpp: Two peers agree on a shared secret with ECDH, derive a session key from it with HKDF-SHA-256 and talk over AES-256-GCM. The raw ECDH output is not a key: HKDF turns it into one and ties it to this application with a context string.
- example/ecdsa_der.cpp: Signs with ECDSA the way a domain library does: a sighash computed by the library, a 64-byte signature, its strict DER form for the wire, and the low-S rule. The same signature has a twin with S replaced by n - S; accepting both makes transaction ids malleable, so verifiers refuse the high-S twin.
- example/ed25519_sign.cpp: Signs RFC 8032's second Ed25519 test with a key pair made from its seed and verifies the signature with the public key alone; then signs the message "abc" given in two pieces with Ed25519ph, as RFC 8032's Ed25519ph test does, and verifies it. Prints each key and signature in hex.
- example/equal_hmac.cpp: Checks an HMAC-SHA-256 tag from Boost.Hash2 with webcpp::crypto::equal, the constant-time comparison. Comparing tags with == or memcmp stops at the first difference, and that timing lets an attacker guess a valid tag one byte at a time.
- example/failure_reasons.cpp: Shows the three ways AES-GCM can refuse a message: a tampered ciphertext, an IV of the wrong size and a tag of the wrong size. A program must tell the first from the others: only authentication_failed means someone changed the data, and open then wipes the plaintext so that no unauthenticated bytes are ever used.
- example/file_share.cpp: A file-sharing app shares a file with a recipient it knows only by an X25519 public key: the file is sealed once in a secret box under a key drawn for this file, and that file key is sealed to the recipient's public key in a sealed box. The upload holds both; only the recipient's secret key opens the file key, and the file key opens the file. Prints what the recipient reads, the sizes on the wire, and the refusals of a changed upload and of another key pair.
- example/key_formats.cpp: Reads RFC 8410's Ed25519 private key in PEM (section 10.3), as OpenSSL or WebCrypto export it, writes its public key as PEM, which is the RFC's section 10.1 to the character, and signs with it; writes an X25519 key pair's public key the same way; and refuses the RFC's version 2 of the private key, which carries the public key too. Prints the PEM texts and each verdict.
- example/kx_session.cpp: A chat app's client and server, each with a crypto_kx key pair made from libsodium's kx test's seeds, exchange public keys and compute their session keys; the client seals a message with its transmit key and the server opens it with its receive key, on ChaCha20-Poly1305; a peer key of low order is refused. Prints the public keys and the client's session keys in hex.
- example/openssl_memory.cpp: Sends every allocation of OpenSSL's to the program's own memory resource, natively, then seals and opens one block with AES-256-GCM on OpenSSL, on a worker thread as an audio engine's or a server's would. Built with WEBCPP_CRYPTO_OPENSSL_MEMORY_RESOURCE, /webcpp/crypto//openssl and threads (example/Jamfile).
- example/order_reference.cpp: Turns a sequential order id into an opaque 16-byte reference with the raw AES block cipher, and back. Customers then cannot guess other orders' numbers. This is NOT authenticated encryption: a forged reference still decrypts, to garbage, so the program checks the padding.
- example/reset_token.cpp: Draws a 32-byte password-reset token and a six-digit one-time code from the system's random generator. Tokens that can be guessed or repeated let an attacker take over accounts, so both come from random_device, never from rand() or the clock.
- example/schnorr_sign.cpp: Signs BIP340's first test vector with secp256k1 and verifies it, then tweaks the key pair by a 32-byte tweak, as a domain library derives one, and signs and verifies under the tweaked key. Prints each key and signature in hex.
- example/sealed_records.cpp: Seals data in pieces two ways: one message in chunks with the incremental seal, and a stream as separate records, each bound to its position and to whether it is the last. The number in the additional data stops records from being reordered or replayed at another position, and the last-record flag stops a stream from being cut short without being noticed. Each stream has a key of its own, drawn when the stream starts: the counter IVs 0, 1, 2 of one stream are safe only because no other stream seals under its key.
- example/signed_message.cpp: An author signs a message with a BIP340 Schnorr signature and a reader verifies it with the author's public key alone. No server vouches for the message: any change to the text breaks the signature, so peers can trust what they receive from untrusted relays.
- example/signed_update.cpp: Checks an update with the publisher's ECDSA signature before installing it. The public key is shipped inside the program, so a tampered download, or one from a mirror that is not the publisher, fails the check and is never run.
- example/store_token.cpp: Stores a user's API token encrypted in a database row, bound to the user's id. The id is additional data: authenticated but not encrypted, so a row copied to another user's record no longer opens. Without that binding a database writer could swap the rows of two users.
- example/taproot_tweak.cpp: Tweaks an internal key as Bitcoin's Taproot does for a key-path-only output (BIP341): the tweak is a tagged hash of the internal key, and the output key commits to it. The same tweak applied to the key pair lets the owner sign for the output key, so spending needs no script.
- example/wallet_key.cpp: Makes a wallet's key pair from a random secret, then seals the secret at rest with AES-256-GCM and restores it. A secret that sits unencrypted on disk, or lingers in memory after use, is the first thing an attacker looks for, so the copies are wiped as soon as they are not needed.
- example/x25519_agree.cpp: Alice and Bob of RFC 7748 section 6.1 agree a shared secret from each other's public keys; then two Ed25519 key pairs, made from RFC 8032's seeds, agree one through their X25519 forms; and a peer key of low order is refused. Prints each public key and the shared secrets in hex.
- example/xchacha_seal.cpp: A chat app, in the browser and natively alike, encrypts each message of a conversation under the conversation's key with XChaCha20-Poly1305, a fresh 24-byte nonce drawn at random per message and the conversation's id as additional data; a message changed on the way, or moved to another conversation, does not open. Prints what the recipient reads.
